note: Lifted semantic model, Lattice (data-centre fabric) side. Home-grown, no standard vocabulary. Lattice (the physical leaf/spine fabric) and the overlay SDN controller are adjacent domains that touch only where the overlay binds to the underlay on a leaf. Concepts carry a bespoke label, synonyms, a kind, a gloss, an example, the ad-hoc reference entry bound to (ref; a native-only concept binds to a native-gap ref), relations, and instances. Carries the 'zone' trap (availability-zone) and one opaque tag. ref=null marks an opaque item.

concepts.label: fabric-attachment
concepts.gloss: the point on a leaf switch where an overlay segment is bound onto a local fabric VLAN and port
concepts.example: the attachment of tenant-blue traffic on leaf-3 port et-9

concepts.label: fabric-vlan
concepts.gloss: the local VLAN on a leaf that carries one tenant broadcast domain within the fabric

concepts.label: leaf-switch
concepts.gloss: a leaf (top-of-rack) switch where servers and overlay bindings attach to the fabric

concepts.label: fabric-mtu
concepts.gloss: the MTU the fabric enforces, sized to carry encapsulated overlay frames without fragmentation
concepts.example: 9216-byte MTU across the fabric for VXLAN overhead

concepts.label: svi-gateway
concepts.gloss: the L3 gateway interface for a fabric VLAN, giving tenant hosts their default route

concepts.label: spine-switch
concepts.gloss: a spine switch forming the fabric backbone between leaves - a fabric-internal object with no overlay counterpart
concepts.example: spine-1 interconnecting all leaves in pod-A

concepts.label: availability-zone
concepts.gloss: an availability zone: a physical fault domain of the fabric (power/cooling/pod boundary) over which placement is spread - a fabric-internal notion of a 'zone', unrelated to any policy grouping
concepts.example: AZ-1 comprising pod-A's racks on independent power
